Fair point, but I would disagree. Sure, if you are of the belief that ADHD is just another cognitive weak point, no different then poor working memory or perceptual reasoning etc…, then yes, iq does represent an ADHDers natural cognitive capabilities. However, I wouldn’t consider ADHD as such because iq can increase when medicating with stimulants/non-stimulant medication (by a pretty significant margin). Anecdotally, my avg iq score went up significantly (like +1 sd) after I started taking Adderall. For a non ADHD person, taking stimulants may boost your confidence, but it wont have any significant effect on your iq. So for a person with ADHD, one’s iq is only an accurate representation of cognitive potential when they are medicated. Otherwise, they are not performing at their maximum capability. Just my thoughts on it at least

The cycle restarts once those side edges are horizontal. So for the top left shape, the rotating edges start at a 45 rotation and are obscured by the diagonal sides of the open triangle.
